Questions we hear

How long does a first visit take?

About an hour, with time for questions at the end. Bring a notebook if you like to write things down.

  • Coffee is on the house.
  • The door opens at nine.

Can I bring someone along, such as a colleague who has never been here before?

Yes. Tell us how many you will be, so that there are chairs enough.

What does it cost?

Nothing for the first visit.

In depth

  1. The first part
  2. The second part
  3. The third part, which has a long name

The first part

Every guide begins somewhere. This one begins with the things you need before you start, which are fewer than you would think: a place to sit, an hour and a question you want answered.

Write the question down. It will change as you go, and that is the point.

The second part

Now look for what others have written. Keep a list of where you found each thing, since you will want to go back.

When the list is long enough, stop. A list never ends by itself.

The third part, which has a long name

Read the list again and cross out what does not answer your question. What is left is your guide.

That is all there is to it.

A crosshead

What did you find?

That most of the work lies in the questions, not in the answers. Once the question was right, the answer came by itself, more or less.

It took a while to see it. For a long time we asked the same thing in different words, and got the same answer each time.

In short

Three things to remember

What the study found, in brief.

  • Ask one question at a time.
  • Write the answers down the same day.
  • Read them again a week later, when they have settled.
